text:
sara: FYI I'm seeing recurring p99 spikes on hosted-prod-us-west2 around 10:30 PDT, ~3x above SLO. microbatch=8, avg latency ~= 130ms but p99 jumps to ~950ms for short bursts. creating thread to collate traces and hypotheses :thinking:

devon: can you attach the trace/trace id? also which kernel was picked in those requests? p99 often correlates with kernel fallbacks or kv thrash. :eyes:

sara: trace id `trace-prod-20260315-1030` pasted here, quick paste from the profiler: 
```
seq_len_hist: p50=64 p90=420 p99=1800
kernel_selected: fused_flash_attention_v2 (default) -> but fallback observed to cpu_attn when kv_size > 1.1M
microbatch_size=8
kv_evictions/sec: 240 -> spikes to 1400 during event window
prefix_cache_hits: 2%
```
link: https://internal.perf/prof/trace-prod-20260315-1030 :link: 

liam: ran a short perf on replica-3 during a repro window. logs show repeated tool-call appends causing the input buffer to grow across generator steps: 
```
2026-03-15T10:30:12Z request-id=R1 user=acct-452 step=gen tokens_out=18 tool_call=search -> appended result size=512
2026-03-15T10:30:12Z request-id=R1 step=gen tokens_out=12 tool_call=search -> appended result size=512
2026-03-15T10:30:12Z request-id=R1 step=gen tokens_out=22 tool_call=search -> total_seq=1580 -> kernel fallback
```
pattern: looped tool results inflating seq_len mid-generation. this triggers kv cache churn since keys are growing and not reused.

priya: I dug into cache telemetry — eviction rate lines up with the spike window. when eviction/sec > 600 we see kernel fallback events and higher p99. prefix caching is disabled for route `/chain/toolcall` (likely because tool outputs flagged as non-deterministic).

priya: quick numbers from A/B: with microbatch=8 & no prefix-cache: p50=120 p95=260 p99=950; with microbatch=2 & prefix-cache enabled (warm) p50=140 p95=300 p99=620. so microbatch down reduced p99 but increased p50 slightly.

sara: confirmed — I rolled microbatch->2 for the problematic route in a canary and p99 dropped ~35% for that route. tradeoff acceptable for these customer routes.

devon: nice. can we make heuristics automatic? e.g., if runtime detects seq_len growth > threshold OR repeated tool-call pattern, reduce microbatch and pin to low-latency kernel pool. also fallback avoidance: we should try to keep kv entries below kernel fallback threshold by preferentially evicting large ephemeral keys.

priya: sketched a heuristic: 
```
if seq_len > 1024 or tool_call_loop_detected(request):
  microbatch = max(1, default_microbatch/4)
  prefer_pool = low_latency_pool
  enable_prefix_cache(tool_result_key) // TTL short
```
tool_call_loop_detected ~= repeated tool_call type > 2 within same generation and appended result size > 128 tokens.
```

liam: also saw a small number of outlier generations where model sampling produced extremely long continuations (token runaway). those are rare (~0.2%) but expensive. grep output: `grep -c "generated_tokens>2000" prod-logs -> 1247 in 7d` and they cluster around certain prompts (system+long-context).

sara: so root causes summary: 1) long prompts / admin flows causing large seq_len, 2) tool-calling loops that append results mid-gen and bypass prefix caching, 3) rare sampling runaway that creates kernel fallback. combined effect produces multiplicative p99 spikes.

devon: mitigation plan: short-term: route known long-prompt flows to dedicated low-latency pool, reduce microbatch for tool-heavy routes, enable short-ttl prefix caching for tool outputs. mid-term: implement loop-detection in preprocessor + adaptive microbatching + eviction policy that prefers ephemeral large keys. long-term: add model-side sampling caps and per-request generation token budget enforcement.

priya: I opened an RFC for adaptive heuristics: https://stash.internal/rfcs/infra/adaptive-microbatch-2026 (WIP). also added telemetry flags to track loop-detection hits and prefix-cache warm ratios.

liam: tests I'd like to run: synthetic workload that mixes 1) long prompts, 2) tool-loop traces replay, 3) high-sampling temperature outliers; measure p50/p95/p99 and kernel-fallback counts. will push a small harness to qa cluster.

sara: thanks — can everyone +1 on the short-term changes? I'll canary deploy microbatch=2 & prefix-cache-ttl=30s to two pods at 11:15 PDT and monitor p99.

devon: +1
priya: +1 (already tested locally)
liam: +1 (will run harness after canary)
deploy-bot: deploy/user=sara action=canary start target=prod-us-west2/pods=[r-3,r-7] id=canary-20260315-1115 :rocket:

sara: canary started. monitoring dashboard: https://internal.console/dashboards/slo/p99?window=15m

sara: initial canary results after 10m: p99 for route dropped from 920ms -> 610ms, kv_eviction/sec steady at ~180, kernel_fallbacks down from 14->3. will keep watching for 1h then roll if stable. :thumbsup:

devon: great. follow-up action items: 1) make adaptive heuristics opt-in per-route, 2) add metric for "tool-loop-detection" to alert before p99 degrades, 3) prioritize eviction policy tweak in next sprint.

priya: I'll file the tickets and put estimated effort. thanks all!
